body:
Someone had this [issue](https://github.com/Zylann/godot_heightmap_plugin/issues/447) too with my plugin. So far my built-in shaders "worked around" it because they didn't use `NORMALMAP` or `TANGENT`, though arguably it's more a legacy thing than a proper approach nowadays.

A project setting would not be ideal in my case because that requires the user to turn it off for their project manually, which is annoying for a plugin, and would hide occurrences where it would actually be useful elsewhere.

If there was a way to avoid triggering this warning by actually checking that the shader *does not read normals from vertex data*, I think it would be better? (since the issue comes from the fact the shader wants to read data from a source that isn't actually provided). I also recall this problem is intertwined with the way Godot wants to compress mesh data in memory, which requires tangents to be bundled in? But in custom use cases where such format isn't even necessary, then it would be pointless to have that warning (or if vertex data is totally absent, think rendering without vertex buffers)

Thanks for the input @Zylann ! I'm not sure how much it is desired, but one could disable this warning using a render mode, similar to how the rendering behavior of shaders is modified. For example:

```
shader_type spatial;

render_mode no_warn_tangents;
```

Not sure if this is desirable, maybe @Calinou could shed some light on this since he commented on #84875 which is tangentially (ha-ha) related. I'd be happy to implement whichever solution is acceptable to get rid of this specific error filling up the logs unnecessarily and slowing down the game while the main thread is busy writing logs.

It's also worth noting that there's also a proposal open in [godot-proposals#10471](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10471), but I think a specific solution to a specific problem would be more desirable as the proposed log message filter may be to generic to go anywhere. I believe, the issue that needs to be resolved is the fact that, while well intended, this warning is factually inaccurate and there should at least be a way to disable this behavior if it needs to be kept. (Alternatively, it could be replaced with a warning in the documentation as is done in other cases as a beginner is unlikely to run into this issue. Mesh generation in combination with shaders isn't exactly a day-1 game dev topic.)

I've been doing some additional digging if it is possible to make the shader evaluation a bit smarter. Unfortunately, that particular rabbit hole leads to this part of the shader compiler:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/19bb18716ef08b811fec330cba4d35fbdb027bcc/servers/rendering/shader_compiler.cpp#L898-L901

The way I read it, it basically just checks if a certain node is being used in the shader code and sets the flag accordingly. Adding an evaluation if the code actually sets the values rather than just reading them would make this code a lot more complicated, which is probably not worth it. Otherwise, one could check if the `TANGENT` is being written to and disable this warning.

Quick and dirty prototype, I'll test it properly before submitting a PR.

Each of the [constant Mesh.ARRAY_MAX] elements contains an array with some of the mesh data for this surface as described by the corresponding member of [enum Mesh.ArrayType] or [code]null[/code] if it is not used by the surface. For example, [code]arrays[0][/code] is the array of vertices. That first vertex sub-array is always required; the others are optional. Adding an index array puts this surface into "index mode" where the vertex and other arrays become the sources of data and the index array defines the vertex order.  				The [param lods] argument is a dictionary with [float] keys and [PackedInt32Array] values. Each entry in the dictionary represents an LOD level of the surface, where the value is the [constant Mesh.ARRAY_INDEX] array to use for the LOD level and the key is roughly proportional to the distance at which the LOD stats being used. I have a strong preference for having a flag on the ArrayMesh itself

> Logically, the tangent generation in shader should be a property of the shader, not the mesh that's being used. Theoretically, you could use the same mesh with a shader that generates tangents and with one that doesn't where the warning would be justified.

The warning is on a per-surface basis and only triggers if the mesh surface has a shader attached that reads/writes from `TANGENT` (or uses it internally from `NORMAL_MAP` etc.). If the shader doesn't touch `TANGENT`, then the warning will not be triggered. _Logically_ the error is attached to the mesh surface, so the flag to disable the warning should be attached to the mesh surface. 

More importantly though, _practically_ this error can occur when using a StandardMaterial3D. I do not want to expose a flag in StandardMaterial3D to disable a mesh error. Nor do I want users to have to go through every material in their project that may use that mesh in order to disable the warning. 

This problem only occurs for user-generated meshes. Internal meshes and imported meshes all have tangents force-enabled, so they don't need to be checked.

I had a hard time reproducing this issue until I re-read [this comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/106276#issuecomment-2870815427) by @clayjohn above:

> After we added the warning, we added code that forces the creation of tangents when importing meshes, so we no longer have the issue with imported meshes. It is just with manually created meshes.

It looks like this isn't the whole story: tangents are generated for manually created meshes (`ArrayMesh.create_surface_from_arrays` and `SurfaceTool`) as well. Tangent generation happens inside `RenderingServer` [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3badc0ee23caf1e5269fe90f8ee17e09d4d2b682/servers/rendering/rendering_server.cpp#L572) when attribute compression is enabled, and [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3badc0ee23caf1e5269fe90f8ee17e09d4d2b682/servers/rendering/rendering_server.cpp#L690) if it's not.

The only way I could find to get a mesh without tangents, is to omit the normals as well.

Since importing a mesh without normals seems quite rare, I wonder if the warning couldn't simply be removed?

Or maybe we should warn when generated tangents are actually used for anything? They are arbitrarily chosen, and unlikely to be what the artist intended.

---

In any case, to fix the immediate issue, we don't need the user to specify any flag. Using `write_flag_pointers` used by the shader compiler, it's easy to check whether `TANGENT` is actually being _written_ to by the shader, and omit the warning accordingly.

It's not perfect (what if the write is conditional? what if it depends on a read?) but similar limitations apply in other parts of shader introspection as well, so I think it's fine for now.
